tapeLine: US stocks ended a mixed Wednesday: the Dow fell 443.87 points (0.9%) to 50,906.05, the S&P 500 lost 0.3% to 7,651.54 and the Nasdaq Composite rose 0.2% to 26,861.06, per AP via ABC News and CNBC. For September the S&P 500 fell 0.5%, the Dow 4.3% and the Nasdaq rose 1.9%; for the third quarter the S&P gained 2%, the Nasdaq 2.5% and the Dow lost 2.7%, per CNBC. August PCE inflation rose 3.4% year on year against 3.7% expected, with core PCE at 3.0%, also below forecasts, per CNBC and DailyForex; Q2 GDP was revised up to 2.2% from 1.5%, per InvestingLive. The 10-year yield sat near 5.29% and the 30-year near 5.63%, per Tradingeconomics-type quote pages. Thursday futures rose after Micron beat and raised guidance: Nasdaq 100 futures +1.0%, S&P 500 +0.6% in early trade, per TradingView News and ATFX.
matters:
Wednesday's data cut against Tuesday's growth-weakness question: PCE inflation came in below forecasts (headline 3.4% vs 3.7% expected, core 3.0%) while Q2 GDP was revised up to 2.2% from 1.5%, per CNBC, DailyForex and InvestingLive. Yet the 10-year stayed near 5.29%, so the softer inflation print did not visibly pull yields lower in sources found. The Fed-hike thread carried since 18 September stays open with the 28 October FOMC the decision point.

Thursday leans on tech: Micron reported fiscal Q4 EPS of $33.42 on revenue of $54.23B against estimates of $31.83 and $51.49B and raised its Q1 outlook, per TradingView News and ATFX; index futures rose in early trade. Iran confirmed on 30 September it received a US response to its seven-day Hormuz proposal via Qatari mediators; contents were not disclosed, per Fortune and CBS News.

Invalidation: Thursday's ISM Manufacturing (10:00 ET) and jobless claims, Friday's jobs report, the contents of the US reply to Iran, and the 10-year yield's behaviour around 5.29%.

regime.sizing: The Fed-hike thread stays open, with the 28 October FOMC the decision point. The Iran thread has a US reply of undisclosed content. Thursday's ISM and Friday's jobs report are the next tests.

secondOrder: Softer inflation did not visibly move the 10-year, which stayed near 5.29%, so the rates thread looks driven by more than the latest PCE print. That is an observation, not a forecast.

scorecard.text: Wednesday's brief carried early futures as little changed to slightly lower. The Dow closed down 0.9% and the S&P 500 down 0.3%, a larger drop than 'slightly' for the Dow, while the Nasdaq rose 0.2%, per AP and CNBC.
Wednesday's brief named the 10-year's behaviour around 5.29% as a test. It stayed near 5.29% through the PCE release, per Tradingeconomics.
Wednesday's brief said no US response to Iran was confirmed. That held at publish time; Iran confirmed receipt of a response later on 30 September, per Fortune.

Wednesday's brief asked whether weak confidence and openings data would change the Fed thread. PCE came in below forecasts but the 10-year did not fall; Thursday's ISM and Friday's jobs report remain.
